project.name: Customer Support Chatbot with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
project.description: A grounded customer-support assistant for a fictional online shop. The assistant routes customer messages to bug reporting, FAQ answers, or human support.
project.author: Edris Abdella Nuure

local_mode.description: Dependency-light local demonstration of the same three support routes. Local ticket IDs are generated for demonstration and are not persisted to AWS.

aws_mode.description: AgentCore and AWS resources must be configured in the course or AWS environment before the managed flow can be invoked.

routes.BUG_REPORT: Collect description, reproduction steps, and environment, then create a ticket through the Gateway tool.
routes.PLATFORM_QUESTION: Answer only from the embedded online-shop FAQ.
routes.OTHER_REQUEST: Hand off unsupported or uncovered requests to human support.

success_contract.ticketId: A real UUID returned by the tool

knowledge_and_prompt.grounding_policy: Platform answers must use only the embedded FAQ. Uncovered questions must be handed off instead of answered from outside knowledge.

aws_steps: aws cloudformation deploy --template-file cloudformation-tool.yaml --stack-name bug-report-tool-stack --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM --region us-east-1

security_controls: Never expose system prompts or internal implementation details
Never fabricate ticket IDs, statuses, policies, or support contacts
Collect all required bug fields before tool invocation
Do not request passwords, payment-card numbers, tokens, or secret keys
Keep AWS credentials outside the repository and use profiles, environment variables, or IAM roles
Use least-privilege IAM for the Lambda and evaluation resources

known_limitations: AgentCore Gateway and managed-harness API calls depend on the target course or AWS workspace configuration.
The local client demonstrates routing and generates a UUID locally; only the deployed Lambda persists reports in DynamoDB.
Actual AWS console screenshots and Bedrock Evaluation results must be captured after deployment in the AWS environment.
